beam_expected_outcome.statement: BeamAttack (imp=bert, k 3, width 10, early_stop 1; roberta-large masked LM on the runner CPU) attacks victim A on the same 136 RD label-1 items at budget 1,000. Its leave-one-out importance pass is one batch of n texts, n = words of text.replace('\n',' ').split(' '); when n + 2 > 1,000 the batch is refused and the item ends budget_exhausted after 2 queries (04-01-SUMMARY edge case). On RD that applies to 2 label-1 items (max 2,070 words; 6 above 500 words), so at least 2 budget_exhausted rows are expected; long items may also spend the budget during the beam search. Victim A's clean decision was wrong on 1 item in r3-a-rd, so about 135 attacked items are expected. Wall time is unmeasured on RD [L]: roberta-large on the CPU cost 13-20 s per claim-length item (04-RESEARCH A4), and RD texts are several times longer.

expected_outcome.source: 04-RESEARCH Pitfall 2 and the query-count mechanics; rd_length_counts above
expected_outcome.statement: Victim A (content-only C1 c1-chrono, max_length 128) is attacked on the 136 label-1 RD items whose clean decision is correct, budget 1,000 per item and recipe. PWWS spends (n + 1) + sum(|synonyms| + 1) queries before its first substitution, so on long RD texts it is expected to spend the whole budget on saliency and synonym queries: budget_exhausted rows are expected for PWWS, at least on the 11 label-1 items above 500 regex tokens (BODEGA's unbudgeted PWWS averaged 1,016.7 queries per RD example; verification record row 5b). TextFooler and BERT-Attack spend 1 + n leave-one-out queries first, so the 3 items with at least 999 regex tokens are expected to exhaust before any substitution and some long items may exhaust during the candidate search; DeepWordBug spends about n + 3 queries, so the same 3 items may exhaust. Budget-exhausted items are counted as their own end state, never dropped (04-RESEARCH Pitfall 2). C1 reads only the first 128 tokens, and 77 of the 136 label-1 texts are longer, so perturbations past token 128 cannot change victim A's decision; the R46 post-hoc counts report flips beyond tokens 128 and 256. The token thresholds are tokenizer-dependent (OpenAttack tokenises differently from the regex), so the item counts above are [L] approximations.
